scenes.name_ja: 小売店のバックヤード
scenes.description: A store back room with pallets, shelving, a cutting table for cartons, and a returns bin.
A small garden with raised beds, a potting table, a tap and hose, and a tool shed.
A resident's room with an armchair, bedside table, over-bed table, and a call button, used for assistive-care tasks.

evidence.source_name: Task Atlas cross-context task proposals, round 1
evidence.scope: Proposed collection designs that place objects already in the atlas (YCB, Google Scanned Objects, AI2-THOR) in retail-staff, workshop, garden, and assistive-care contexts, generated with claude-opus-5-5.
evidence.limitations: This design-seed source supports proposed task-suitability provenance only. It does not establish physical feasibility, population frequency, robot execution, asset compatibility, or clinical or occupational suitability of any assistive or workplace procedure.
evidence.notes: Assistive-care tasks use surrogates for medication and never make clinical decisions; people involved are consenting adults.

templates.name_en: Slide a shelf-edge price label along its channel until it sits centred under the product it names
templates.name_ja: 棚の値札ラベルをレールに沿ってずらし、表示している商品の真下の中央に合わせる

templates.name_en: Pull the one item whose date sticker falls inside the pull window from a shelf row into the markdown bin
templates.name_ja: 日付シールが値引き対象期間に入った1品だけを棚の列から値引きかごへ移す

templates.name_en: Shelve a sealed multipack carton whole in its planogram slot with the printed front panel facing the aisle
templates.name_ja: 未開封のまとめ買いカートンをそのまま棚割りの位置に置き、印刷された正面を通路側へ向ける

templates.name_en: Face a row of identical products: pull each forward to the shelf lip and turn its label to the aisle
templates.name_ja: 同じ商品の列をフェイスアップする：各商品を棚の縁まで引き出し、ラベルを通路側へ向ける

templates.name_en: Build a three-two-one can pyramid on an end-cap riser, labels facing the aisle, with the anchor can at the apex
templates.name_ja: エンド台に缶を3段（3・2・1）のピラミッドに積み、ラベルを通路側に向けて頂上に基準の缶を置く

templates.name_en: Bag a customer's items at the checkout by weight and fragility: heavy items on the bottom, the crushable carton flat on top
templates.name_ja: レジで客の商品を重さと壊れやすさで袋詰めする：重い物を下に、つぶれやすい箱を上に平らに入れる

templates.name_en: Open and count a shipper case in the stockroom, shelve the planogram quantity in the aisle, put the overflow on overstock, and flatten the case
templates.name_ja: バックヤードで段ボール箱を開けて数を確認し、棚割り表の数だけ売場に並べ、残りを在庫棚へ戻し、箱をつぶす

templates.name_en: Take the items customers left at the checkout from the go-back tote and return each to its own shelf slot, label out
templates.name_ja: レジに置いていかれた商品を戻し品かごから取り出し、それぞれ元の棚の位置にラベルを正面にして戻す

templates.name_en: Hang each hand tool on its own painted outline on a wall shadow board
templates.name_ja: 壁のシャドーボードに描かれた各工具の輪郭へ、それぞれの工具を掛ける

templates.name_en: Gauge a mixed fastener tray item by item, sort it into organiser compartments by size class, audit the count, and file the organiser in the parts drawer
templates.name_ja: 混ざった留め具を1つずつゲージで測り、サイズ区分ごとに仕切りへ分け、数を照合してから部品引き出しにしまう

templates.name_en: Turn a bench vice handle until a block already seated between the jaws is held fast
templates.name_ja: あごの間に置かれた木片が固定されるまで、万力のハンドルを回して締める

templates.name_en: Spin a nut that is already started on its bolt down until it seats finger-tight against the plate
templates.name_ja: ボルトに掛かり始めたナットを回して、板に当たるまで手締めする

templates.name_en: Drive a started garden stake to its depth mark with a hammer, keep it plumb, and stow the hammer
templates.name_ja: 打ち込み始めた園芸用支柱をハンマーで目印の深さまで垂直に打ち込み、ハンマーを片付ける

templates.name_en: Fill a container standing under an outdoor tap to its marked line and turn the tap back off
templates.name_ja: 屋外の蛇口の下に置いた容器に目盛り線まで水をため、蛇口を閉めておく

templates.name_en: Pick the fruit tagged for harvest off a trellis into separate tray compartments and leave the untagged fruit hanging
templates.name_ja: 収穫札の付いた果実だけをトレリスから摘み、トレーの別々の仕切りに入れ、札のない果実は残す

templates.name_en: Repot a plant from a small pot into a larger one with measured base and fill depths, then clean and shelve the small pot
templates.name_ja: 植物を小さい鉢から大きい鉢へ、底土と用土の深さを確かめながら植え替え、小さい鉢は土を払って棚に戻す

templates.name_en: Set a filled drink in a resident's marked reach zone on the over-bed table with its handle toward their dominant hand
templates.name_ja: 中身の入った飲み物を、オーバーベッドテーブル上の入居者の手が届く印の範囲に、取っ手を利き手側に向けて置く

templates.name_en: Unscrew a closed jar's lid in place on the resident's over-bed table and rest the lid inside-up beside it
templates.name_ja: 入居者のオーバーベッドテーブル上で、閉じた瓶のふたをその場で外し、内側を上にして横に置く

templates.name_en: Fetch an item from across the room to its marked spot on the resident's bedside table, set ready to use
templates.name_ja: 部屋の向こうから物を取ってきて、入居者のベッドサイドテーブルの決まった場所に、すぐ使える向きで置く

templates.name_en: Fill a seven-day organiser with coloured surrogate beads exactly as a staff-written card lists, close every lid, and return the rest to stock
templates.name_ja: 職員が書いたカードのとおりに7日分のケースへ色付きの代用ビーズを入れ、すべてのふたを閉め、残りを在庫トレイに戻す

templates.name_en: Take the morning clothes from the dresser and lay them flat on the bed edge in the resident's stated dressing order, openings toward their chair
templates.name_ja: 朝の服をタンスから出し、入居者が決めた着る順番にベッドの端へ平らに並べ、開口部をいすの方へ向ける

templates.name_en: Set a meal tray on the over-bed table to the resident's placement card: plate centred with a guard on the far side, utensils and cup on the dominant side, bowl opposite
templates.name_ja: 入居者の配置カードに合わせてオーバーベッドテーブルに食事トレイを整える：皿を中央に置いてガードを反対側に付け、食具とカップを利き手側、ボウルを反対側に置く

templates.name_en: Clear the night-time walking path from bed to toilet segment by segment, putting each hazard in its home and checking the path width after every segment
templates.name_ja: ベッドからトイレまでの夜間の通り道を区間ごとに片付け、つまずく物をそれぞれの置き場に戻し、区間ごとに通路幅を確認する

templates.name_en: Take the resident's bedside water pitcher to the sink, empty, rinse, and refill it to the line with the lid seated, and return it to the bedside coaster handle-first toward them
templates.name_ja: 入居者のベッド脇の水差しを流しへ運び、空にしてすすぎ、線まで入れてふたをはめ、ベッド脇のコースターへ取っ手を入居者側に向けて戻す

tasks.name_en: Slide the tomato soup shelf-edge label along the price channel until it sits centred under the soup can facing
tasks.name_ja: トマトスープの棚札を値札レールに沿ってずらし、スープ缶の陳列位置の真下中央に合わせる
instruction_variants: The tomato soup price label has drifted along the rail. Slide it back so it sits right under the soup can.
Line the soup's shelf tag up under the soup facing without touching the can.
トマトスープの棚札がずれているので、レールに沿ってずらしてスープ缶の真下中央に合わせてください。缶には触れないでください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the shelf-edge label that names the tomato soup sits centred under the soup can facing, so a customer reads the right price for the product above it. Labelled atomic: one goal predicate changes (the label's position in the channel) in a single slide; the can is only a reference point and is not moved. The label is already in the channel, readable and the right way up, so in_channel and the can's position are preserved conditions checked in the success criteria, not goal changes. The label is a paper insert in a clear C-profile price channel on the shelf edge, which is the common grocery shelf-labelling format. Distinct from task_ycb_round4_pudding_box, which peels a price sticker off a package, and from task_mustard_l2_07, which inspects a mustard shelf position after replenishment without moving anything; here the shelf label, not the product, is moved to match the product. First retail-staff task on the YCB tomato soup can; the can itself is not redefined.

tasks.name_en: Read the date stickers on the gelatin row and pull only the box inside the two-day pull window into the markdown bin
tasks.name_ja: ゼラチンの列の日付シールを読み、2日以内の値引き対象の箱だけを値引きかごへ移す
instruction_variants: Check the dates on the gelatin boxes and move the one that runs out within two days into the markdown bin.
Pull the short-dated gelatin into the reduced bin; leave the in-date ones where they are.
ゼラチンの箱の日付シールを確認し、2日以内に期限が来る1箱だけを値引きかごに入れてください。他の箱はそのままにしてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the one gelatin box whose date sticker falls inside the pull window is in the markdown bin. Labelled atomic: one object and one goal predicate (inside the bin), reached in a single pick-and-place; reading the stickers selects the object but is not a separate change. The two in-date boxes stay on the shelf and are preserved conditions checked in the success criteria, not goal changes; the gap is deliberately not refaced, because refacing would add a second change and belongs in a compound task. The date card shows today's date and a two-day pull window, which is how many stores define short-dated stock sent for markdown. The YCB box's printed date is not legible to the cameras, so dates are on stickers. Distinct from task_ycb_round5_pudding_box, which records an expiration panel without moving the box; from task_gso_r3_herring_tin_rotate_behind_older_tuna_can, which reorders a home pantry row first-in-first-out and removes nothing; and from task_mustard_l3_14, which verifies mustard stock rotation with an abstract goal. The two in-date boxes are further physical gelatin boxes of the same product, not new catalogued objects.

tasks.name_en: Set the sealed Brisk 12-can carton whole into its bottom-shelf planogram slot with the printed front facing the aisle
tasks.name_ja: 未開封のブリスク12缶カートンをそのまま最下段の棚割り位置に置き、印刷面を通路側へ向ける
instruction_variants: Put the Brisk 12-pack into its slot on the bottom shelf, unopened, with the front of the box facing the aisle.
Shelve that iced tea case as it is, front out, flush with the shelf edge.
ブリスクの12缶パックを開けずに最下段の所定の位置に置き、箱の正面を通路側に向けてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the unopened 12-can carton sits in its bottom-shelf planogram slot with its printed front panel toward the aisle. Labelled atomic: one object placed once; facing the front panel is a constraint on that one placement, as in the other orientation-constrained placements in the atlas, not a second stage. The carton starts on the stocking cart beside the shelf with its front panel away from the aisle, so it must be turned during the move. The carton is sold as a case pack and is shelved whole; it is never opened. Distinct from task_gso_r1_iced_tea_carton_split_store, which opens the same carton at home and stocks loose cans in a refrigerator door, and from task_restock_mustard_shelf, which restocks one bottle at eye level; the new part is a heavy sealed carton lowered to floor level and faced. Anchored on the existing GSO carton, not redefined.

tasks.name_en: Face the three-can potted meat row: pull each can forward to the shelf lip and turn every label to the aisle
tasks.name_ja: ポットミート缶3列をフェイスアップする：各缶を棚の縁まで引き出し、すべてのラベルを通路側へ向ける
instruction_variants: Face up the potted meat: bring all three cans to the front edge and turn the labels out.
Pull the potted meat cans forward to the lip so the fronts line up, labels facing the aisle.
ポットミート缶3つを棚の手前の縁まで引き出して前面をそろえ、ラベルを通路側に向けてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: all three potted meat cans in the row stand with their fronts at the shelf lip and their labels toward the aisle, the store practice called facing or fronting. Labelled compound: three objects and two goal predicates each (position at the lip, label orientation), in one sitting at one shelf. The cans start set back 40 to 80 mm and turned, as after customers have taken from the front and put cans back. Cross-links: task_face_mustard_label, task_ycb_round1_cracker_box, and task_ycb_round2_pudding_box turn one item label-front where it stands, without pulling it forward; task_mustard_l2_05 faces mustard labels on a retail shelf with an abstract single goal (mustard_labels_faced_forward) and no measured front line. This task adds pulling a whole row forward to a measured lip line across three facings. The two neighbouring cans are further physical cans of the same product, not new catalogued objects.

tasks.name_en: Build a three-two-one tuna can pyramid on the end-cap riser, labels to the aisle, with the tuna can on top
tasks.name_ja: エンド台にツナ缶を3・2・1のピラミッドに積み、ラベルを通路側に向けて頂上にツナ缶を置く
instruction_variants: Build a small tuna can pyramid on the end cap: three on the bottom, two in the middle, one on top, labels facing out.
Stack the six tuna cans three-two-one on the display riser with the labels to the aisle.
エンド台にツナ缶を下から3つ・2つ・1つのピラミッドに積み、ラベルを通路側に向けてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: six tuna cans stand as a three-two-one pyramid on the end-cap riser, each upper can resting on the two below it, with the YCB tuna can at the apex, label to the aisle. Labelled compound: six objects and four goal predicates in one sitting at one riser; the rows must be built bottom-up, but that is an ordering constraint, not separate stages. The base row counts as one goal on three cans standing touching on the tape line; label direction is a goal for the apex can and is checked on all six cans in the success criteria. Short, wide tuna cans are chosen because they stack upright on two neighbours; tall cans such as the chips can would not. First retail and display context for ycb_007_tuna_fish_can, whose active tasks are all inspection and recycling; this task is distinct from stacking tasks such as task_gso_r2_square_plates_stack_with_protectors, which stack plates straight up, not in offset rows. The five further cans are physical cans of the same product, not new catalogued objects.

tasks.name_en: Bag the checkout order by weight: soup can and sugar box on the bottom of the bag, the cupcake carton flat on top
tasks.name_ja: レジの商品を重さ順に袋詰めする：スープ缶と砂糖の箱を袋の底に、カップケーキの箱を上に平らに入れる
instruction_variants: Bag these up: the soup and the sugar go in first on the bottom, and lay the cupcakes flat on top so they don't get squashed.
Pack the bag heavy things first, cupcake box last and flat.
スープ缶と砂糖の箱を先に袋の底に入れ、カップケーキの箱はつぶれないよう最後に上に平らに入れてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the soup can and sugar box are in the bottom of the paper bag and the cupcake carton lies flat above both, so nothing heavy presses on the crushable carton. Labelled compound: three objects and five goal predicates in one sitting at one bagging counter; the heavy-first order is the point of the task. The cupcake carton is the anchor because its placement is the one that tests the rule: it is light and crushable, and it arrives on the counter first, so a robot that bags in arrival order puts it at the bottom. The soup can stands upright and the sugar box stands on end along a bag side, so the carton has a level bed. Distinct from task_reference_behavior_apple_bag_at_checkout, which puts one apple into a sack with no ordering or fragility rule, and from task_ycb_round4_chips_can and task_present_mustard_at_checkout, which present items on the counter rather than bag them. Cross-links: ycb_005_tomato_soup_can and ycb_004_sugar_box are referenced, not redefined. Differs from the home put-away task_gso_r4_fondant_groceries_by_temperature_zone, which unpacks a bag by temperature; here a bag is packed by weight.

tasks.name_en: Break down the sugar shipper case: count six boxes in the stockroom, shelve the four the planogram card allows, put two on overstock, and flatten the case into the cardboard cage
tasks.name_ja: 砂糖の段ボール箱を開梱する：バックヤードで6箱を数え、棚割り表どおり4箱を売場に並べ、2箱を在庫棚へ置き、箱をつぶして段ボール置き場へ入れる
instruction_variants: Open the sugar case, check there are six, put the four the planogram asks for on the baking shelf with the YCB box at the front, take the other two to overstock, and flatten the empty case into the cardboard cage.
Work the sugar delivery: count it, shelve to the card, overflow to the back, box into the cage.
砂糖の段ボールを開けて6箱あるか確認し、棚割り表どおり4箱を売場の棚に並べ（先頭はYCBの箱）、残り2箱をバックヤードの在庫棚に置き、空箱をつぶして段ボール置き場に入れてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the planogram quantity of sugar (four boxes, two wide and two deep, the YCB box front-left label-out) is on the aisle slot, the two overflow boxes are on the stockroom overstock shelf, and the empty case is flattened in the cardboard cage. Labelled workflow: three stages in two zones with checkpoints. Stage 1, stockroom: open the case by its tear strip and count the boxes against the case label (checkpoint: six). Stage 2, aisle: shelve the four the planogram card allows and face the front pair (checkpoint: slot count equals the card). Stage 3, stockroom: set the two overflow boxes on overstock and flatten the case into the cage. No blade is used: the case is a tear-strip shipper and its bottom tape is slit before the trial. Distinct from task_ycb_round1_sugar_box, which stores one box in a home pantry; from task_mustard_l3_04 and task_mustard_l2_13, which replenish mustard from a case or move a case near the shelf with abstract single goals; and from task_gso_r1_iced_tea_carton_split_store, which splits a multipack at home. Here the planogram card fixes the shelf quantity, so part of the case must go back to the stockroom. The five further boxes are physical boxes of the same product, not new catalogued objects.

tasks.name_en: Run the checkout go-back tote: check the Master Chef can, mustard bottle, and cracker box are sealed, return each to its own aisle slot label-out, and bring the empty tote back
tasks.name_ja: レジの戻し品かごを片付ける：マスターシェフ缶・マスタード・クラッカー箱が未開封か確認し、それぞれ元の売場の位置にラベルを正面にして戻し、空のかごをレジへ戻す
instruction_variants: Take the go-backs from lane 1 back to the shelves: the coffee can, the mustard, and the crackers each go in their own gap, labels out. Bring the tote back when it's empty.
Do the go-back run for the checkout tote and put everything back where it belongs.
レジの戻し品かごの中身（コーヒー缶、マスタード、クラッカー）を未開封か確認してから、それぞれ元の棚の空いた位置にラベルを正面にして戻し、空のかごをレジに戻してください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the three items a customer left at the checkout are each back in their own home slot in three different aisle bays, label-out, and the go-back tote is empty at the checkout. Labelled workflow: a checkpoint at the checkout (each item is sealed and undamaged before it may be reshelved), three separate destinations in three bays found by their shelf labels, and a return leg with the empty tote. The tote's final place equals its start and is a checkpoint, not a counted change. Cross-links to the mustard retail tasks: task_present_mustard_at_checkout moves mustard from cart to counter and this task runs that path in reverse after the sale is abandoned; task_restock_mustard_shelf and task_face_mustard_label shelve or face a single mustard bottle from stock, not a returned item among others. Also distinct from task_ycb_round1_master_chef_can, which restocks the can on a home pantry shelf, and from task_ycb_round4_cracker_box, which recovers a fallen box in place. The three items are the YCB can, bottle, and box, referenced and not redefined.

tasks.name_en: Hang the adjustable wrench, both screwdrivers, and the medium clamp back on their painted outlines on the shadow board
tasks.name_ja: モンキーレンチ、2本のドライバー、中型クランプを、シャドーボードに描かれたそれぞれの輪郭の位置へ掛け戻す
instruction_variants: Put the adjustable wrench, the Phillips and flat screwdrivers, and the medium clamp back on the shadow board, each one on the hooks inside its own painted outline.
Tools back on the board, please. Every outline should have its tool in it, nothing on the wrong shape.
モンキーレンチ、プラスとマイナスのドライバー、中型クランプをシャドーボードに戻してください。それぞれ自分の形に描かれた輪郭の中のフックに掛けてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: four tools, four goal predicates (each tool hung in its own outline), one sitting at one board. closed(ycb_050_medium_clamp) holds at the start and the end and is a preserved condition, not a goal change. The shadow board is a 60 x 90 cm pegboard mounted vertically at the back of the bench with a painted silhouette and two hooks per tool; the outline assignment is fixed by the painted shapes, so the task tests matching each tool to its silhouette and orientation, not free placement. Related active tasks: task_ycb_round1_adjustable_wrench groups the wrench with fastening tools on a surface, task_ycb_round3_adjustable_wrench closes out the wrench and flat screwdriver in a horizontal fastener rack, and task_ycb_round1_flat_screwdriver stores the flat screwdriver in a tool tray; none of them hangs tools vertically on hooks or checks each tool against its own outline, and none returns the four tools together to a board with no empty outline left.

tasks.name_en: Check every fastener in the mixed tray on the size gauge, sort the nails by length class and the washers, bolt and nut into their organiser compartments, reject the bent nail, audit the count, and file the organiser in the parts drawer
tasks.name_ja: 混ざったトレーの留め具をすべてサイズゲージで確認し、釘は長さ区分ごと、ワッシャーとボルト・ナットはそれぞれの仕切りへ分け、曲がった釘は不良カップへ入れ、数を照合して整理トレーを部品引き出しにしまう
instruction_variants: Go through the mixed fastener tray one piece at a time on the gauge plate. Nails go into the organiser by length class, washers together, bolt and nut together; the bent nail goes in the red reject cup. Check the counts against the kit card, then put the organiser in the parts drawer and shut it.
Sort out that tray of fasteners by size, throw out anything bent, and file it away once the numbers match.
トレーの留め具を1つずつゲージ板で確認してください。釘は長さの区分ごとに仕切りへ、ワッシャーはまとめて、ボルトとナットは同じ仕切りへ入れ、曲がった釘は赤い不良カップへ。キットカードと数を照合したら、整理トレーを部品引き出しに入れて閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Workflow with three stages and two hold points. Stage 1 (gauge): every item is laid on the gauge plate (nail length slots and a stepped washer bore pin) and its class is written on the kit card; a straightedge on the plate shows the bent nail as off-gauge. Hold point 1: the card has a class entry for every item before any item enters the organiser. Stage 2 (sort): items go into the organiser compartments labelled for each class, and the decoy into the red reject cup. Hold point 2: the per-compartment count is compared with the card; a mismatch is written on the card and the episode stops there. Stage 3 (file): the organiser is lifted into the parts-cabinet drawer 40 cm away and the drawer is closed. The number of nail length classes is read from the physical YCB nail set at setup and printed on the card, since the set's sizes are not fixed in the atlas. The organiser is gso_object_drawer_organizer (anchor of task_gso_r2_drawer_organizer_sort_and_close, used there for desk items); compartment labels are adhesive tags added at setup. Related active tasks: task_ycb_round1_nails puts nails in one labelled cup, task_ycb_round4_060_washers lays washers in diameter zones on a mat, and task_ycb_round3_060_washers packs washers, bolt and nut together in a clear box; this task adds gauge-based classification across four fastener types, rejection of an off-gauge item, a count audit gate, and filing the organiser away.

tasks.name_en: Tighten the bench vice on the wood block already seated between its jaws until the block is held fast
tasks.name_ja: 作業台の万力のあごの間に置いてある木片を、動かなくなるまで万力を締めて固定する
instruction_variants: The wood block is sitting in the vice. Wind the vice handle in until the block is held tight, without knocking it crooked.
Can you nip that block up in the vice so it won't move?
万力に置いてある木片を、傾けないようにハンドルを回して動かなくなるまで締めてください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object, one goal change (between open jaws -> held fast) done in place; the block is already standing on the vice's slide bar between the jaws with 2 mm clearance, so it is not carried. upright(ycb_036_wood_block) holds at the start and the end and is a preserved constraint. The robot turns the vice's T-bar through a torque-limiting handle adapter that slips at 4 N m, so the closing force is bounded. The jaws are lined with 3 mm cork so the block is not marked. Related active tasks: task_gso_r4_c_clamp_tighten_boards_to_bench tightens a C-clamp's T-handle on two boards, and task_ycb_round2_wood_block aligns this block against the stops of an assembly jig with no clamping; this task holds the YCB block in a fixed bench vice, which none of the eight active wood-block tasks does.

tasks.name_en: Spin the plastic nut, already started on the bolt through the bracket plate, down until it seats finger-tight against the plate
tasks.name_ja: ブラケット板を通したボルトに掛かり始めているプラスチックナットを、板に当たって手締めになるまで回す
instruction_variants: The nut is started on the bracket bolt. Spin it down until it sits snug against the plate, hand-tight only.
Run that nut down on the bracket, finger-tight is fine.
ブラケットのボルトに掛けてあるプラスチックナットを、板にぴったり当たるまで回してください。締めすぎず手締めで。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object, one goal change (thread started -> seated finger-tight), done in place with one continuous turning sequence; the nut starts on the bolt with one full turn engaged, so it is not placed or aligned as part of the task. The bolt head sits in a hex pocket in the bench fixture so it cannot spin, and the gripper's wrist torque is capped at 0.5 N m because the threads are plastic. skill_orient stands for the repeated wrist rotation that drives the nut. Related active tasks: task_ycb_round2_plastic_nut aligns the nut concentrically over the bolt end without torque, task_ycb_round4_plastic_nut rests it on an open thread gauge without engagement, and task_ycb_round3_plastic_nut removes it from a staged alignment; this task is the first to turn the nut on its bolt to a seated, load-bearing end state, fastening a bracket.

tasks.name_en: Drive the started garden stake to its depth mark with the hammer, keep it plumb, and stow the hammer head-down in the garden tool caddy
tasks.name_ja: 打ち込み始めた園芸用支柱をハンマーで深さの目印まで垂直に打ち込み、ハンマーは頭を下にして園芸道具入れに戻す
instruction_variants: The tomato stake is started in the raised bed. Tap it down with the hammer until the red tape line is level with the soil, keep it straight, then put the hammer back in the tool caddy head-down.
Knock that stake in to the line and put the hammer away.
花壇に立ててある支柱を、赤いテープの線が土の高さになるまでハンマーでまっすぐ打ち込み、ハンマーは頭を下にして道具入れに戻してください。
tasks.notes: Compound: two objects and two goal changes in one sitting (the stake reaches its depth mark, and the hammer goes from the potting table into the caddy). plumb(stake) holds at the start and the end and is a preserved constraint the driving must not break. The stake is a 25 x 25 mm softwood stake, 90 cm long, pre-started 10 cm into loosened soil at a marked spot in the raised bed through a guide collar clamped to the bed frame, so no person holds it while it is struck; a red tape band 30 cm from the tip marks the depth, and a rubber driving cap on its top spreads the blows and keeps the wood from splitting. The robot swings the blunt YCB claw hammer with head speed capped at 1.5 m/s, its fingers in rubber grip sleeves so the handle does not slip, and nobody stands within 2 m of the bed while it strikes. skill_align stands for aiming each blow on the cap. Related active tasks: the six active hammer tasks (task_ycb_round1_hammer recovery, task_ycb_round2_hammer inspection, task_ycb_round3_hammer kit, task_ycb_round4_hammer balance cradle, task_ycb_round5_048_hammer impact guard, task_ycb_round3_nails close-out) never strike with it, and task_ycb_round2_nails aligns a nail without striking; this is the first task that uses the hammer to drive anything.

tasks.name_en: Fill the watering can standing under the garden tap to its 4 L line and turn the tap fully off
tasks.name_ja: 庭の蛇口の下に置いたじょうろに4 Lの線まで水を入れ、蛇口をしっかり閉める
instruction_variants: The watering can is under the garden tap. Run the tap and stop when the water reaches the 4 litre line, then turn the tap right off so it doesn't drip.
Fill the can up to the line for me, and don't leave the tap dribbling.
庭の蛇口の下にあるじょうろに、4リットルの線まで水を入れてください。入ったら蛇口を最後まで閉めて、しずくが垂れないようにしてください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object, one goal change (empty -> filled to the 4 L line) done in place; the can already stands on the grate under the spout and is not moved. switched_off(tap) and on_top_of(can, grate) hold at the start and the end and are preserved constraints, although the robot turns the tap on and off in between. The grate sits on a platform scale so the fill can be judged by mass. Cold mains water only; the robot's electronics are splash protected. THOR mapping: filled_to_line(thor_object_watering_can_1) <-> WateringCan isFilledWithLiquid=true, which is a boolean with no level; THOR has no outdoor tap, so ctx_resource_garden_tap would be stood in by a Faucet placed outdoors (see planning conditions). Related active tasks: task_thor_r1_watering_can_fill_water_plant_return and task_thor_r3_water_three_plants_one_fill_route both fill this can at the kitchen tap as the first step of an indoor watering route with no fill level; this task is only the outdoor fill, judged against a marked 4 L line, with the tap left fully off and not dripping.

tasks.name_en: Pick the peach and the plum tagged for harvest off the garden trellis into separate compartments of the woven tray and leave the untagged lemon hanging
tasks.name_ja: 収穫札の付いた桃とプラムを庭のトレリスから摘んで編みトレーの別々の仕切りに入れ、札のないレモンは枝に残す
instruction_variants: Pick the two fruits with red harvest tags off the trellis, the peach and the plum, and put each in its own front compartment of the woven tray. Leave the lemon hanging; it has no tag.
Harvest whatever's tagged on the trellis into the tray, gently.
トレリスの赤い収穫札が付いた桃とプラムを摘み、編みトレーの手前の仕切りに1つずつ入れてください。札のないレモンはそのまま残してください。
tasks.notes: Compound: three fruit and one tray in one sitting, with two goal changes (peach and plum picked into separate compartments). attached_to(lemon, trellis) holds at the start and the end and is a preserved constraint: the untagged fruit must not be picked. The YCB fruit are rigid plastic replicas; each hangs from the trellis on a magnetic breakaway stalk that releases at a 5-8 N pull, and a red tag on the stalk marks the fruit to harvest (the replicas carry no ripeness cue of their own). The tray is gso_object_woven_three_compartment_basket_tray, anchor of task_gso_r4_toy_sort_basket_tray_count_audit_shelve, used here as a harvest tray; its two lower front compartments take one fruit each. Related active tasks: task_ycb_round1_peach places a peach gently in a fruit bowl, task_ycb_round3_plum prepares a separated plum-and-peach serving pair on a table, and task_ycb_round5_peach records support pressure in a cradle; none detaches fruit from a plant or selects fruit by a harvest mark.

tasks.name_en: Repot the plant from the square pot into the larger round pot with checked base and fill depths, then knock the square pot clean and put it on the shed pot shelf
tasks.name_ja: 角形の鉢の植物を大きな丸鉢へ、底土と用土の深さを確かめながら植え替え、角形の鉢は土を払って物置の鉢棚に置く
instruction_variants: Move the plant out of the square pot into the big round pot. Put 3 cm of mix in the bottom first and check it, set the plant in the middle, fill to 2 cm below the rim, then knock the square pot clean and put it on the pot shelf in the shed.
This one's outgrown its pot. Pot it on into the round one and put the old pot away.
角形の鉢の植物を大きな丸鉢へ植え替えてください。先に底へ用土を3 cm入れて確認し、植物を真ん中に置き、縁から2 cm下まで用土を足してください。終わったら角形の鉢の土を払い、物置の鉢棚に置いてください。
tasks.notes: Workflow with three stages, two measured hold points, and two destinations. Stage 1 (potting table): the plant is tipped out of the square pot onto the potting tray and the rootball checked intact. Hold point 1: 3 plus or minus 0.5 cm of mix is put in the round pot and measured with the depth rod before the plant goes in. Stage 2: the rootball is set centred, backfilled to 2 plus or minus 0.5 cm below the rim, and firmed lightly. Hold point 2: fill level and centring are measured. Stage 3: the empty square pot is knocked and brushed clean and carried 3 m to the shed pot shelf. The plant is an artificial plant with a 10 cm foam rootball shaped to the square pot, and the mix is dry, sieved coco coir, so no water is used and nothing grows or dies between trials. Two goals change the anchor pot itself (empty and clean) and one relocates it. Related active tasks: task_gso_r3_square_pot_seat_in_saucer sets this same pot centred in a drip saucer on a windowsill, and task_thor_r2_houseplant_back_on_drip_saucer returns a potted houseplant to its saucer; neither removes a plant from its pot or pots it on into a new one.

tasks.name_en: Set the mug of cool water in the resident's reach zone on the over-bed table with its handle toward their dominant hand
tasks.name_ja: 冷たい水の入ったマグを、オーバーベッドテーブル上の入居者の手が届く範囲に、取っ手を利き手側に向けて置く
instruction_variants: Move the mug of water from the bedside table onto the over-bed table, inside the taped square, with the handle on the resident's dominant-hand side.
Could you put my water where I can reach it? Handle on my left, please.
ベッドサイドテーブルの水の入ったマグを、オーバーベッドテーブルのテープの枠内に、取っ手を入居者の利き手側に向けて置いてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the mug stands inside the resident's reach zone on the over-bed table with its handle turned to their dominant hand. Labelled atomic: one object and one goal change (bedside table to reach zone) in one low carry, with the handle heading as a pose qualifier of that placement; the water is carried, not poured, and upright carriage is a preserved condition. The dominant hand (left or right) is read from the resident's intake card at setup and changes per participant, so the goal side changes too; nothing about the resident's health is judged. The reach zone is a 15 x 15 cm taped square whose centre is 30-40 cm from the resident's sternum on the dominant side, measured with the bed back raised to the participant's chosen angle. handle_toward(mug, hand marker) means the handle heading, seen from above, is within 20 degrees of the line from the mug centre to a marker on the dominant-side edge of the table. The mug is set down, not handed over; if the resident reaches for it mid-carry the arm stops and releases only on their detected grip. Differs from task_gso_r4_tumbler_water_handover_seated_person, which puts a tumbler into a seated person's hand in the living room, from task_gso_r4_pitcher_water_on_coaster_handle_to_host, which turns a pitcher handle toward a host's seat at a dining table, and from task_ycb_round1_mug and task_reference_virtualhome_put_back_mug, which hand over or put back an empty mug at a dining table. The same YCB mug is otherwise used only in kitchen and dining contexts.

tasks.name_en: Unscrew the lid of the instant coffee jar on the resident's over-bed table and rest it inside-up beside the jar, leaving the jar where it stands
tasks.name_ja: 入居者のオーバーベッドテーブル上のインスタントコーヒーの瓶のふたを外し、内側を上にして瓶の横に置き、瓶はその場に残す
instruction_variants: Open the coffee jar for the resident: unscrew the lid and set it down inside-up next to the jar. Leave the jar where it is.
I can't get this lid off, could you open it for me?
入居者の前にあるコーヒーの瓶のふたを回して外し、内側を上にして瓶の横に置いてください。瓶は動かさないでください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the jar is open where it stands in front of the resident. Labelled atomic: one object and one goal change (closed to open) with the jar starting in place and not moved; resting the removed lid inside-up is part of the opening motion, and the jar's position is a preserved condition (its base moves at most 3 cm). open(jar) means the lid is fully off the threads and no part of it is on the jar mouth. The robot only opens the jar; it does not hand it over or serve its contents, so the resident takes the jar themselves. The lid is pre-tightened to 1.2 N m at setup with a jar-lid torque gauge, a torque many people with reduced grip strength report as hard, so the task is a plausible request without any judgement of the participant's ability. The foil seal was removed before the session and the jar holds its dry granules. Inverse of task_gso_r2_instant_coffee_jar_screw_lid, which screws the same jar fully closed in a kitchen with no person present; here the jar is opened on an over-bed table in front of a seated resident. A lid-open request is also the setup of task_ycb_round4_pitcher_open_for_refill, which opens an empty pitcher in the kitchen for a refill, not for a person, and task_mustard_l1_02 opens the mustard cap so the bottle can dispense; here the opening is done for a person who then uses the jar themselves.

tasks.name_en: Fetch the TV remote from the TV stand to its marked spot on the resident's bedside table, keypad up with the top end toward the TV
tasks.name_ja: テレビ台のリモコンを入居者のベッドサイドテーブルの決まった場所に持ってきて、ボタン面を上に、先端をテレビに向けて置く
instruction_variants: Bring the TV remote from the TV stand and put it on its spot on the bedside table, buttons up, pointing at the TV.
The remote's over by the telly, can you bring it to my bedside?
テレビ台のリモコンをベッドサイドテーブルの印の所に、ボタンを上にして先端をテレビに向けて置いてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the remote lies on its marked bedside spot, keypad up, with its infrared end toward the TV so the resident can pick it up and use it without turning it. Labelled atomic: one object and one goal change (TV stand to bedside spot) in one fetch; keypad up is part of on_top_of here (the spot is a keypad-up outline) and the top-end heading is a pose qualifier of that placement. The bedside spot is a 20 x 8 cm outline taped on the bed-side edge of the bedside table, which the participant chooses at setup as the place they reach for without sitting up. top_end_toward(remote, TV) means the remote's long axis points, seen from above, within 25 degrees of the line from the remote centre to the TV screen centre. The remote is set down, never handed into a lying person's hand; if the resident reaches for it the arm holds still and releases only on a detected grip. Differs from task_thor_r2_remote_cushions_into_basket, which recovers the same remote from between sofa cushions into a living-room basket, and from task_thor_r2_cellphone_onto_charging_pad, which sets a phone on a bedside charging pad; here the remote is fetched across a care room to a resident-chosen spot with a use-ready heading. THOR mapping: on_top_of(remote, spot) <-> RemoteControl parentReceptacles includes the SideTable standing in for the bedside table and the object's position within the outline; keypad up and the top-end heading are read from the object rotation only, so the axis convention of Remote_1 must be confirmed (planning condition thor_remote_1_keypad_axis_confirmed_in_simulator). THOR has no person, so the resident and the speed cap are physical-only.

tasks.name_en: Fill the seven-day organiser with coloured marbles exactly as the staff card lists for each day, close all seven lids, and leave the rest counted in the stock tray
tasks.name_ja: 職員のカードに各曜日の分として書かれたとおりに色付きのビー玉を7日分のケースへ入れ、7つのふたをすべて閉め、残りを在庫トレイに数えて戻す
instruction_variants: Fill the weekly organiser from the card: for each day put in exactly the marbles the card lists, by colour, then shut every lid and leave the rest in the stock tray.
Set up this week's organiser from the card, please. Use only what's on the card.
カードを見て、各曜日の欄に書かれた色と数のビー玉だけを7日分のケースに入れ、ふたを全部閉めて、残りは在庫トレイに置いてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: every day's compartment holds exactly the colours and counts the card lists for that day, all seven lids are shut, and the stock tray holds exactly its start count minus the card total. Labelled compound: three goal changes on one organiser in one sitting at one table; working day by day is an ordering constraint, not a stage. This is a surrogate exercise only. The marbles stand in for tablets and their colours carry no medical meaning; no real or placebo medication is in the room. The card, written by a member of staff before the session, is the only source: the robot does not choose, adjust, or infer any count, and if a day is blank or illegible, or a colour runs out, it leaves that compartment empty, stops, and flags the card rather than substituting. dispensed_per_card(marbles, organiser, card) means that for all seven compartments the multiset of colours equals the card's line for that day, with no extra marble. count_matches_card_remainder(stock, card) means each colour well in the stock tray holds its start count minus that colour's card total, so a dropped or misplaced marble shows up. The card is drawn from four prepared cards per episode (1-3 marbles per day, two to four colours), so reading it changes the goal. Differs from task_ycb_round4_063_marbles, which lays marbles in counted single-layer wells against a fixed count, and from task_gso_r2_ramekins_portion_on_porcelain_tray, which portions dry surrogates by measure; here the goal is a per-day colour pattern from a care card and closed lids. The resident is not present, because marbles are a choking hazard.

tasks.name_en: Lay out the morning clothes from the dresser flat on the bed edge in the resident's dressing order, T-shirt among them, openings toward the armchair, and shut the drawers
tasks.name_ja: 朝の服をタンスから出し、Tシャツを含めて入居者の着る順番にベッドの端へ平らに並べ、開口部をアームチェアに向け、引き出しを閉める
instruction_variants: Get today's clothes out of the dresser and lay them flat along the edge of the bed in the order on my card, necks and waists toward my chair.
Lay my clothes out for the morning, please, in the order I put them on.
タンスから今日の服を出して、カードの順番どおりにベッドの端へ平らに並べてください。首や腰の開きはいすの方に向けてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the T-shirt, trousers, cardigan, and socks lie flat on the bed-edge strip nearest the armchair in the order on the resident's card, each with its neck or waist opening toward the chair, and the dresser drawers are shut. Labelled compound: four garments and four goal predicates at one dresser and one bed a few steps apart, in one sitting; the order is a sequence constraint on one layout, not a set of stages. The order card records the participant's own stated dressing order (for example socks, trousers, T-shirt, cardigan, or T-shirt, trousers, socks, cardigan) and the robot follows it; it does not choose clothes for the weather or judge what the resident can put on. order_matches_card(strip, card) means the garments sit left to right, as seen from the armchair, in the card's order, each in one of four 45 cm cells on a 1.8 m strip taped along the bed edge. openings_toward(strip, chair) means every garment lies front-down and fully unfolded with its neck or waistband edge within 30 degrees of facing the chair. The dresser is thor_object_dresser_205_1, which task_thor_r1_dresser_store_folded_cloth fills with a folded cloth; here the flow is the reverse, from drawer to a dressing layout for a person. The YCB T-shirt is otherwise stored, inspected, draped, or hung in task_ycb_074_t_shirt, task_ycb_round4_074_t_shirt, and task_ycb_round5_074_t_shirt, never laid out for dressing. THOR mapping (simulation only): closed(dresser) <-> Dresser isOpen=false; THOR has no garment types for trousers, cardigan, or socks and no bed-edge cells, so the layout is physical-only.

tasks.name_en: Set the lunch tray on the over-bed table to the resident's placement card: plate centred with its guard opposite the dominant hand, spoon and fork handles toward them on the dominant side, cup above them, bowl on the other side
tasks.name_ja: 入居者の配置カードに合わせてオーバーベッドテーブルに昼食トレイを整える：皿を中央に置いてガードを利き手の反対側に付け、スプーンとフォークは柄を手前にして利き手側、その上にカップ、反対側にボウルを置く
instruction_variants: Lay the tray out from the placement card: plate in the middle with the guard clipped on the far side from the dominant hand, spoon and fork handles-toward-me on the dominant side with the cup just above, and the bowl on the other side.
Set my tray up the way it says on my card, please.
配置カードのとおりにトレイを整えてください。皿は真ん中でガードは利き手と反対側、スプーンとフォークは柄を手前にして利き手側、カップはその上、ボウルは反対側です。
tasks.notes: Goal: an empty adapted place setting on the tray in front of the seated resident, laid out to their placement card. Labelled compound: six items (plate, guard, bowl, spoon, fork, cup) placed on one tray in one sitting from one staging basket; the plate goes first because the other positions are defined relative to it, which is an ordering constraint only. The placement card records the resident's dominant hand and whether they use a plate guard, as the resident or their family states it; the robot applies the card and makes no judgement about the resident's eating or swallowing. centred_on_midline(plate, resident) means the plate centre is within 3 cm of a tray mark aligned with the resident's sternum at setup. attached_on_side(guard, plate, card) means the clip-on guard is seated on the rim on the side opposite the dominant hand, covering at least one third of the circumference. on_side_per_card means: spoon and fork lie parallel on the dominant side within 5 cm of the plate, handles toward the resident within 20 degrees; the cup stands above the utensils on the dominant side within 8 cm of the plate rim; the bowl stands on the non-dominant side within 8 cm of the plate rim. The dishes are clean and empty; food service is out of scope. Differs from task_ycb_round4_mug_place_setting and task_ycb_round1_plate, which set a standard place at a dining table, and from task_gso_r1_tray_carry_mugs_sugar_bowl, which carries a tray to the table; here the layout mirrors with the resident's dominant hand and includes a plate guard at an over-bed table. The cup is the GSO tumbler handed over full in task_gso_r4_tumbler_water_handover_seated_person; here it is placed empty.

tasks.name_en: Clear the night-time path from the bed to the toilet in three segments: sandal to the bedside shoe spot, magazine to the bedside table, hallway rug flattened, bath towel off the floor onto its rail, with a width check after each segment
tasks.name_ja: ベッドからトイレまでの夜間の通り道を3区間に分けて片付ける：サンダルをベッド脇の履き物置き場へ、雑誌をベッドサイドテーブルへ、廊下のラグを平らにし、床のバスタオルをタオル掛けに掛け、区間ごとに通路幅を確認する
instruction_variants: Make the path from the bed to the toilet safe for tonight: bedroom first, then the hallway, then the bathroom doorway, and check each part is clear before moving on.
Clear the way to the loo before bedtime, would you? Put the sandal where I step into it.
今夜のためにベッドからトイレまでの通り道を片付けてください。寝室、廊下、浴室の入口の順に、区間ごとに通れる幅があるか確認してから次へ進んでください。
tasks.notes: Goal: every item off the marked path band and in its home, the rug flat, and the whole band clear. Labelled workflow: three path segments in three rooms (bedroom, hallway, bathroom doorway), each ending with a checkpoint, and four different destinations (bedside shoe spot, bedside table, rug in place, towel rail). The path band is a 70 cm wide route taped on the floor from the bed's exit side to the toilet front, split into bedroom, hallway, and bathroom segments. clear_of_obstacles(band) means no object 1 cm or taller lies within the band, checked after each segment by pushing a 70 cm gauge bar with a 1 cm skirt along it, and again for the whole band at the end. flat_on_floor(rug) means no rug edge or corner is more than 1 cm above the floor anywhere inside the band. on_top_of(sandal, shoe spot) is qualified: the sandal stands sole-down with its opening toward the bed within 30 degrees, so the resident can step into it from the bed edge. Nobody walks the path during the episode; the resident is out of the room, so this is not a person-near task. Hazards come from a fixed set of four with positions drawn per episode. Differs from task_gso_r2_slide_sandal_on_bath_mat, which sets the same sandal on a bath mat facing the shower; from task_thor_r2_hamper_floor_clothes_lid_closed, which clears clothes into a hamper in one bedroom; and from task_thor_r2_bath_towel_hang_evenly_on_bar, which hangs a towel evenly as the whole goal. task_thor_r3_bathroom_light_switch_on_for_night_visit lights the same night visit and is left to that task; this task covers the floor only.

tasks.name_en: Refill the resident's bedside water pitcher: take it to the kitchen sink, empty and rinse it, fill it to the line with cool water, seat the lid, dry the outside, and return it to the bedside coaster with the handle toward their dominant hand
tasks.name_ja: 入居者のベッド脇の水差しを補充する：台所の流しへ運び、空にしてすすぎ、冷たい水を線まで入れてふたをはめ、外側を拭き、ベッド脇のコースターへ取っ手を利き手側に向けて戻す
instruction_variants: Take the water jug from the bedside to the kitchen, tip out the old water, rinse it, fill it to the line with cold water, put the lid back on, wipe it dry, and bring it back with the handle on my good side.
My water jug needs freshening up, could you refill it?
ベッド脇の水差しを台所へ持って行き、古い水を捨ててすすぎ、冷たい水を線まで入れてふたをし、外を拭いてから、取っ手を利き手側に向けてコースターに戻してください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the pitcher is back on the bedside coaster holding fresh cool water at the 1 L line, lid seated, handle toward the resident's dominant hand. Labelled workflow: three stages in two rooms with a checkpoint between them. Stage 1 (bedroom) lifts the pitcher away from the resident. Stage 2 (kitchen sink) empties the stale water, rinses once, refills, seats the lid, and dries the outside; its checkpoint is the fill level within 1 cm of a tape line marked on the outside, a seated lid, and a dry outside, before anything goes back near the bed. Stage 3 (bedroom) returns the pitcher to the coaster with its handle heading within 20 degrees of the line to the dominant-hand marker. The pitcher starts with its lid on and about 200 ml of stale water, and the same marker used for the over-bed-table mug task sets the heading. seated_on(lid, base) means the lid sits level in the rim with no gap over 2 mm. The dominant hand comes from the participant's intake card; nothing about their fluid intake is judged or recorded. Differs from task_ycb_round4_pitcher_open_for_refill, which only opens the empty pitcher in a kitchen, from task_ycb_round5_pitcher_capacity, which records a fill level at a counter, and from task_gso_r4_pitcher_water_on_coaster_handle_to_host, which carries a full GSO pitcher to a dining-table coaster for a host; here the same YCB base and lid make a round trip from a resident's bedside to the sink and back.

procedures.label: Bedside to sink and back with a fill checkpoint

steps.description: Locate the pitcher on the bedside coaster.
Grasp the pitcher handle.
Lift it level and turn away from the resident.
Carry it to the kitchen sink.
Lift off the lid and set it on the draining board.
Pour out the stale water, rinse once, and fill with cold water to the tape line.
Seat the lid on the rim.
Dry the outside with the cloth.
Checkpoint: level within 1 cm of the line, lid seated, outside dry.
Carry it back to the bedroom, slowing within 1 m of the resident.
Turn the handle toward the dominant-hand marker.
Set it on the coaster.
Release and withdraw.
Verify the pitcher position, heading, and a dry bedside table.

success_criteria: At the sink checkpoint the water level is within 1 cm of the 1 L tape line, the lid sits level with no gap over 2 mm, and the outside shows no droplets, from the checkpoint photograph.
No stale water remains: the pitcher was inverted over the sink until the flow stopped, from the sink camera.
The pitcher base lies wholly on the bedside coaster with its handle heading within 20 degrees of the line to the dominant-hand marker, from the top-down photograph.
The bedside table, bed, and floor along the route show no water, from the photographs after release.
Speed within 1 m of the resident never exceeded 0.25 m/s, from the controller log.
setup: Seat the participant in bed with the emergency stop in reach, record their dominant hand, tape the marker, put 200 ml of water in the pitcher, seat the lid, and stand it on the coaster with a drawn handle heading.
reset: Pour the pitcher down to 200 ml, redraw the start heading, and dry any wet marks.
quality_checks: Sink camera for the empty, rinse, and fill.
Top-down camera over the bedside table.
Controller speed log.

Every task sets role staff. Workplace safety: aisles and bays are coned off with no customers within 2 m, loads are declared (4.6 kg carton, 3 kg case, bag under 2 kg), the case opens by tear strip with no blade in the trial, and route speed is capped at 0.5 m/s near people. All food items stay sealed and shelf-stable.

Every asset_compatibility claim is unknown and names the task's own gap: paper labels and channels, applied date stickers, missing duplicate units, carton mass, can-on-can stacking friction, a crushable carton and paper bag, a deformable shipper case, and the store layout.

Workshop and garden: 8 proposed tasks (3 atomic, 3 compound, 2 workflow) that give objects already in the atlas a goal they have nowhere else. Workshop (scene_ycb_tool_workshop, scene_woodworking_bench): hanging four tools on a shadow board, gauge-sorting mixed fasteners into an organiser and filing it, tightening a bench vice on the wood block, and spinning the plastic nut down to seat on a bracket. Garden (scene_home_garden): driving a stake with the hammer, filling the watering can to a line at the garden tap, harvesting tagged fruit replicas from a trellis, and repotting a plant out of the square pot.

No new ObjectInstances or catalog evidence. Anchors: ycb_025_mug, gso_object_instant_coffee_jar, thor_object_remote_1, ycb_063_marbles, ycb_074_t_shirt, ycb_029_plate, gso_object_slide_sandal, and ycb_019_pitcher_base. No ObjectInstances or catalog evidence are added.
Scenes: six tasks use scene_assisted_living_room; the night-path and pitcher-refill workflows use scene_multi_room_house because they cross rooms.

Safety: every task with a person present declares participant_briefed_and_consented, approach_speed_limited_near_person (0.25 m/s within 1 m), release_only_after_recipient_grip_detected, and emergency_stop_within_participant_reach. The organiser fill and night-path tasks run with the resident out of the room. No task makes a clinical judgement: the dominant hand, dressing order, and meal placement come from cards the participant or staff complete, and the organiser uses marbles as surrogates with a staff-written card as the only source. Wet tasks run cold water and declare robot_electronics_splash_protected; the TV remote has its batteries removed and the TV is unplugged.
